title: perfcheck.py time defaults to the platform's ceiling in tests_ceiling.json
goal: python3 _tools/perfcheck.py time with no --max-seconds bounds the run by max_seconds of the running platform in _tools/tests_ceiling.json (times KB_TEST_TIMEOUT_FACTOR on a CI runner, as tests.py does), and an explicit --max-seconds still wins, so an item's time check follows the operator's ceiling decision without hand edits. Found in SP-eahtellz: ST-4mcoplex and ST-xjb4wykm said --max-seconds 60 and needed a planning commit when D-776rvpx2 raised the win32 ceiling to 150 s.
